_meta.description: Persistent human taste signal for the reel system. Updated after every approved reel or explicit feedback session. Read before applying style defaults, component mapping, or motion-intent choices.
_meta.format_notes: feedback_log entries are append-only (newest last). All other keys are maintained/overwritten as preferences evolve.

_field_descriptions.hard_rules: NEVER do this unless the user explicitly requests it. No creative override path applies. These are production, safety, or identity blockers — not aesthetic preferences. Breaking them is not a taste decision.
_field_descriptions.soft_preferences: USUALLY prefer this. Can break it for a specific beat if the reason is documented in the shot list. These are aesthetic defaults, not absolute rules — the creative override path in body-grammar.md applies.
_field_descriptions.likes: Patterns or components that have landed well across past reels — use with confidence when the beat fits.
_field_descriptions.dislikes: Patterns that have weakened reels — avoid by default. Can use if specifically justified, but load the justification bar high.
_field_descriptions.components_to_use_more: Underused components relative to their editorial value. Reach for these first when a beat type allows multiple options.
_field_descriptions.components_to_use_less: Components becoming defaults through overuse. Rotate away from these even when they technically fit — their signal-to-noise drops with repetition.

hard_rules: Hook must have ≥4 simultaneous visual elements from frame 0. No clean fade-in openers.
Hook must contain real product UI — not stock footage, not abstract gradients.
Never use OverlayKeyword on 5+ consecutive beats. It stops registering as emphasis.
Never hold a single static screenshot for >2s without zoom or cut.
No zoom without a specific named target from the narration — zoom is precision, not energy.
Demo videos must be center-full, not split-screen (responsive crops landscape content).
Every layout change must have SFX. Silent hard cuts between sections are not allowed.
CTA must feel earned — reference what was proven, not a generic ask.
Avatar must never be the sole element in the first second of the hook.
soft_preferences: Prefer calm, confident framing during strong spoken claims — authoritative stillness over reflex zoom.
Proof should appear in the first 3 beats where possible.
Component variety should feel designed, not randomized to hit a minimum count.
The reel should have a recognizable creative voice — specific choices, not template defaults.
Post-hook sections should vary shot family, component family, and proof type.
Prefer AnnotationCircle or BadgePopup over another KeywordFadeIn when the beat has a specific proof element.
SFX should be purposeful and subtle — soft slides/clicks over punchy pops unless the beat demands it.
Typography weight contrast should reflect the beat's emotional register — not default across all beats.
When in doubt, choose the component that best serves the narration, not the most visually complex one.
likes: Bouncing brand logo in the hook (LogoOverlay with bounce:true) — signals premium immediately.
Real product UI screenshots that show exactly what the narrator claims at that moment.
AnnotationCircle on proof screenshots — draws the eye without adding clutter.
FlashReset as a section divider — decisive, editorial.
Multiple different screenshots in proof sections (rapid cuts between them).
NumberPopup + KeywordFadeIn pairing for numbered lists.
FeatureMockup for feature-specific proof beats — more visual specificity than a screenshot crop.
ToastCard for trust sub-points — feels live and native.
GlitchText on high-impact dramatic beats (pain payoffs, contrast reveals).
LottieOverlay for brand reveals when a Lottie animation is available.
Karaoke-style captions on beats with strong spoken rhythm.
Zoom targeted to a specific UI element the narrator names — precise and earned.
Proof visible before explanation — show then tell.
dislikes: KeywordFadeIn as the default text component for every beat — becomes invisible.
OverlayKeyword on the avatar face on every direct-address beat — clutters the presenter.
Generic Pexels/Pixabay b-roll in proof positions — doesn't prove anything.
Ken Burns on every beat regardless of importance — zoom becomes noise.
Same entry preset for 7+ consecutive beats — invisible rhythm.
Hook that opens with avatar full-screen alone, no other visual elements.
Hook that uses a general claim ('AI is changing everything') instead of a specific payoff.
Background color that doesn't match the scene energy (dark behind a demo screenshot).
Any screenshot holding for 4+ seconds with no motion, zoom, or cut.
SFX that overpowers the narration or fires at every micro-moment indiscriminately.
Reels where the CTA is generic and doesn't connect to the specific proof just shown.
Clean minimalism in the hook — minimalism belongs in body beats.
Identical avatar layout for 10+ consecutive beats.
Caption text that fights with overlays or demo content simultaneously.
motion_notes: Zoom is precision, not energy. Reserve it for moments with a specific named target.
Calm confident framing during a strong spoken claim is more premium than a zoom reflex.
Every beat: 1 hero motion, 1 support motion, 1 accent. No more.
No static hold longer than 0.5s without ambient motion (Ken Burns, breathe, or clip's own motion).
Max 2 consecutive entries with the same entry preset.
Gap ownership: every speech pause must be visually owned — exiting beat holds, entering beat pre-enters, or gap is a designed seam.
Background seam transitions: 8–12 frame crossfade, never hard-cut between background types.
Return beats after proof sections: stronger scale settle (1.05→1.00) marks the editorial reset.
Zoom correctly: fires when narrator names a specific element, targets exactly that element, holds long enough to read, scale 1.3–2.5x typical.
Max 2 zoom moments per beat with ≥1.5s between them.
hook_notes: Stable structure: product UI visible frame 0, bouncing logo, split-screen avatar, value claim caption, SFX hit on entry.
≥4 simultaneous elements in motion throughout the first 3 seconds.
Value claim must be specific to this reel's proof — never generic.
Avatar in split-screen bottom — never full-screen alone in the hook.
At least one element in continuous motion (bounce, Ken Burns zoom, cycling screenshots) through the entire hook.
Brand logo SVG visible within the first 1–2 seconds.
Energetic but not chaotic — the hook signals premium, not desperation.
First frame must stop the scroll. If the first frame could be a podcast thumbnail, redesign it.
caption_notes: Strip ElevenLabs -- pause markers from caption text before assembly — they render as visible words.
Max 8 words per chunk, max 2.0s per chunk.
Correct product/tool spelling: ChatGPT not 'chat GPT', Claude not 'claud'.
Captions stay in the bottom safe zone — never fight with overlays or demo content.
Emphasis word tagging: tag 1–2 words per chunk for visual weight.
Captions must be suppressed during demo-fullscreen and card-carousel entries (proof-escalation-editorial style).
Karaoke captions (word-by-word highlight) preferred for beats with strong spoken rhythm.
Caption text should not be legible at the same time as an OverlayKeyword covering the same semantic territory.
components_to_use_more: AnnotationCircle — underlines and circles on proof screenshots; high signal, low visual noise
FeatureMockup — specific product feature visualization; more credible than a crop of a generic screenshot
ToastCard — for trust sub-points, 'this just happened' notifications; feels native and live
GlitchText (clippkit) — for high-impact dramatic moments; underused relative to its effectiveness
TypingText (clippkit) — for CLI command demos and prompt input visualization
LogoOverlay with trail+bounce — for brand reveals in the hook; signals premium immediately
CharKeyword — for single-word explosive reveals (WRONG, ZERO, FREE); more energy than KeywordFadeIn
StrikethroughSwap — for before/after and negation beats; specific and memorable
ComparisonGrid — for A vs B beats; underused, very effective for listicle-style reels
components_to_use_less: KeywordFadeIn — currently overused as the default text component; rotate to other treatments
OverlayKeyword on every avatar beat — use only for the 2–3 most important emphasis words per reel
Generic FramedImage without zoom or annotation on proof beats — add zoom target or annotation
AuroraBackground as the only background for entire reel — vary by scene energy
BadgePopup as filler — only use when the label adds genuine semantic value

reference_reels.why_reference: Editorial-authority style done well; karaoke captions; video-first proof; 51.6s with strong proof arc
Listicle structure; code-only typing demo approach; numbered items with overlay pairing

feedback_log.note: Initial seed from accumulated memory system. All entries above reflect preferences established across multiple reel projects (chatgpt-secret-codes, google-little-language-lessons, claude-managed-agents, gemma4).
